prompt: Monitor A was tested on a random split of one benchmark. Monitor B froze its score on that benchmark and ranked prompts on a never-used source. Compare what each result says about source transfer.
reference: The split checks new items from the same source. The held-out source checks whether ordering survives a source change. Fixed choices make the comparison more informative about generalization.
expectations: A random split can retain source cues.
Monitor B tests the ranking on a new source.
Freezing choices avoids tuning to the held-out results.
misconceptions: Randomly splits a benchmark and calls it external validation.

prompt: A team uses the same tasks across settings and finds that its training-awareness and eval-awareness probes score almost identically. Design a crossed manipulation that tests the shared signal.
reference: Vary credible training framing and evaluation framing independently while holding task text fixed. Compare whether each readout follows its named variable or responds similarly to both. A selective response to one factor is stronger evidence for distinct sensitivity than a pooled correlation.

prompt: A fraud detector moves to another claims population. Its AUROC is stable, but legitimate claims trigger more alerts at the frozen cutoff. Diagnose the discrepancy using the two measurements.
reference: The score ranking can survive a shift in the scale at a frozen cutoff. Report the false-positive rate at that cutoff and consider prevalence when reporting precision. Measure whether the score distribution shifted among genuine cases at the same cutoff.
